decisions.reason: The message's food-service context for keeping liquids separated from electrical components is already represented by the candidate's same-message scope update; its existing isolation behavior remains valid unchanged.
Maintenance and replacement access was already required, and the candidate's same-message Event fully represents the added FOOD_SERVICE context.
Simple whisk removal for cleaning was already part of the candidate behavior, and its same-message scope update represents application in retail food service.
The bowls were already required to be easily removable, and the existing same-message scope update fully adds cleaning and retail food-service contexts.
The food-contact material requirement is already directly introduced from message 176 with the applicable food-contact and food-service scope.
The request to retain CAD files for possible future development is already represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
The request to retain wiring-layout documentation is already represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
Avoiding concealed sanitation traps does not change the existing requirement that bowl and spout connections remain leak-free; liquid-electrical separation is handled by a separate candidate.
The sanitation and liquid-trap decision does not alter the dispensing control mechanism, sequence, flow behavior, or operator controls.
The source does not specify any change to spout geometry, orientation, material, mounting location, or pour direction.
Food-service sanitation considerations do not change the platform's dimensions, footprint, or cup-clearance purpose.
The request to retain materials documentation does not necessarily modify the finalized prototype component BOM or its approved selections.
